question: The marked price of a table is ₹ 8,980. If the shopkeeper offers a discount of 19%, what is its selling price (in ₹, to the nearest rupee)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The Selling Price (SP) will be exactly (100% − 19%) = 81% of the Marked Price.

SP = 81% of 8980

SP = 0.81 × 8980 = 7273.8

Rounding off to the nearest rupee, we get ₹ 7,274.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 7,274.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹ 8,980

Discount = 19%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 MP
 ₹ 8980
 
 

 − 19% Discount
 
 
 SP
 ₹ 7274

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 8980 × (100 − 19) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 8980 × 81 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 898 × 8.1

⇒ SP = 7273.8

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest rupee, SP ≈ ₹ 7,274

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 7,274.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated by: a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Mark-up Percentage

It is the percentage by which the Marked Price is set above the Cost Price. Formula: Mark-up % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

Direct Relation (MP and CP)

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly written as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
